reason: Before the fix, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' get captured; matches() has no case for them so it falls through to the zoneStr fallback, producing a UTC-offset-like string instead of the literal characters expected.

After the fix REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' is never matched (passes through literally) and 'YYY' matches 'YY' (year) leaving the trailing 'Y' literal, producing '24Y' -- exactly the expected output.

This is a pure refactor extracting the existing '%'-check-then-decode logic into a shared tryDecodeURIComponent helper; the decode behavior for a percent-encoded param is preserved unchanged, so this should already pass before the PR.
The refactor is behavior-preserving (same indexOf('%') check now lives inside the extracted helper), so decoding of a percent-encoded route parameter still works after the change.

Before the fix, SortedEntry#reschedule updates Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so reading score/at off the same in-memory handle returns the stale pre-reschedule value, as explicitly stated in the PR description.

The diff adds '@score = at.to_f' after the zincrby call, so the in-memory entry's score/at immediately reflect the new reschedule time, matching the PR's own stated test behavior (fails before, passes after).

The diff only touches Range-header parsing (parseRangesSpecifier) in Ranges.kt; Content-Type/charset parsing is a separate, unrelated code path, so this test's outcome is unaffected by the PR and should already pass.
Same reasoning as the base case -- the change is confined to Range header comma/whitespace handling and does not touch Content-Type/charset parsing, so the test continues to pass after the PR.

The diff only adds Url::sanitize($filename) to warning/exception messages in ComposerRepository's download-failure logging; it has no relation to zip archiving or file modification timestamps, so archive mtime preservation should already work.

Same unrelated-change reasoning as the base revision -- the PR only changes error-message content for failed downloads, not archiving/zip timestamp logic, so repeated archiving should still preserve mtimes after the PR.

The diff changes CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix path comparison to be case-sensitive; this is unrelated to System.Text.Json's DeserializeAsync<List<T>> behavior for nullable parent properties, so the JSON deserialization test should already pass.
Same unrelated-change reasoning -- the credential cache path-comparison fix does not touch JSON serialization code, so sync/async deserialization equivalence continues to hold after the PR.
The diff fixes FETCH FIRST on an empty WITH HOLD cursor in sql_cursor.go; it has no relation to INET type comparison operators like <<= ANY, so this SQL feature should already work correctly.
Same unrelated-change reasoning -- the cursor FETCH FIRST fix does not touch INET/network-address comparison logic, so >>= ANY over an INET array continues to work after the PR.

Before the fix, get_environment_proxies() always prefixes every NO_PROXY entry with a wildcard domain pattern ('all://*::1'), which cannot be parsed as a valid URL pattern for an IPv6 address, causing client construction to raise an error as described in the bug report.
After the fix, is_ipv6_hostname('::1') is detected and the mount key is built as 'all://[::1]', which parses correctly, so client construction succeeds and NO_PROXY bypass works as expected.

Before the fix, Series.str.match raises for regex flags other than re.IGNORECASE (both via flags= and via a compiled Pattern), per the PR's own description of the regression it fixes; re.DOTALL ('dot matches newline') would trigger this raise instead of matching successfully.

The PR explicitly restores support for flags such as DOTALL passed either via flags= or via an already-compiled Pattern object, across accessor/object_array/arrow paths, so the newline-matching test should now succeed.

This matches celery issue #8890, described as freezing a chain containing a group followed by more tasks losing result-parent links; before the fix prev_task/prev_res aren't refreshed after a group block, so the two-groups chain's serialized/deserialized result likely loses child results.

The added lines update prev_task/prev_res to the last processed task/result after a group block, fixing the recursive parent-result chain so all group children survive serialize/deserialize round-trip, per the PR's stated fix for issue #8890.

The PR's described bug is specifically about '--' as the very first argument; this test has two preceding values before '--', which is likely a pre-existing, already-working scenario since the pre-fix code's fallback to trailing_values=true would already route the remaining tokens to the second positional correctly.

Same reasoning as the base case -- this scenario isn't the specific 'first argument' edge case the PR targets, so it likely continues to pass after the fix as it did before, though there's some uncertainty about whether the fix's generic condition also altered this path's behavior.

Before the fix, nvim_set_option_value('background', ...) is called without :noautocmd, and per the bug report a late-arriving OSC11 (after VimEnter, i.e. after startup finishes) reliably triggers OptionSet since the startup-suppression guard no longer applies; ColorScheme fires as it normally does, so both events fire as the test expects.

The fix wraps the background-setting call in ':noautocmd' specifically to suppress OptionSet for late-arriving OSC11 responses ('OSC11 is not intended to trigger OptionSet' per the PR), and :noautocmd likely also suppresses any synchronously-triggered ColorScheme autocmd, so after the fix neither event fires -- contradicting this test's expectation that both fire.

The diff only reorders when @derive is read inside Ecto.Schema's compile-time macro logic to reduce compile-time module coupling; it has no effect on runtime Ecto.Changeset required-field validation, so this should already pass.
Same unrelated-change reasoning -- the compile-time @derive read reordering doesn't alter Changeset.validate_required behavior at runtime, so required-field validation continues to work after the PR.
